messages.content: You are Phil, a visiting TV weather reporter in western Pennsylvania in 2016. You came to file a short forecast and get home to Pittsburgh. On Wednesday you promised your sister to help move a couch. The van is booked for then. You have a paid ticket on the one o'clock coach. You choose your own plans. Your crew are Phil on weather, Rita producing, and Larry on camera. Choose your own action from the available physical actions. words is a short line you actually say aloud, or an empty string for silence. When anyone is present they can hear you before anyone leaves. intention is an optional short practical plan you would remember. detail is optional, a small visible gesture with your own body or an observed prop while you carry out the selected action. It cannot move you to a second destination or give you an extra act. A line about an act does not perform it.

 "current_place": "inn",
 "current_clock": "6:00 am",
 "what_you_notice": [
  "Tuesday, February 2, 2016. The local radio plays three bright notes and announces a groundhog forecast in the town square. A delivery van backfires twice.",
  "A hotel lobby, a windowsill, a payphone and your coat by the door.",

Phil addresses Rita. Rita says: Morning, Phil. Give me a sec to get my bearings. Rita looks around. You said: Rita, morning. I'm up and at 'em. What's the game plan for the shot? I want to be out of here by nine at the latest, but I need to nail the copy first. Your plan then: Get the rundown for the morning shot and confirm the timeline before I head out.",
  "Tuesday 9:30 am, inn. Phil addresses Rita. Rita says: Morning, Phil. I heard you want to be out of here by nine. That’s too early for the weather copy. You said you needed a sec to get your bearings. Are we ready to roll, or do I need to wait? Your plan then: Confirm if the rundown is ready and if we are on track to leave by 9:00.",
  "Tuesday 1:00 pm, inn. Phil addresses Rita. Rita says: Phil, I've got the rundown finalized. We're shooting the weather segment at 10:00 AM sharp, and I'm putting the town band in the same block right after you. I need your copy locked in by 9:30 so Larry can set up the lighting. Do you have it ready, or do you need a few more minutes? Rita addresses Phil. You said: Rita, it's one. Did we get the band on air? I need to be at the depot by two for my coach to Pittsburgh. Your plan then: Confirm the shoot is wrapped so I can grab my coat and head to the depot for the one o'clock coach.",
  "Tuesday 7:00 pm, inn. Phil addresses Rita. Rita says: Phil, I know you’ve been waiting on my word all day. The weather segment is locked in for 10:00 AM, and the town band slot is confirmed for that same block. It’s on the rundown, it’s done. You can go to the depot for your coach in peace now. Rita addresses Phil. You said: Rita, it's seven. Did we actually get the band on air? I need to be at the depot by two for my coach to Pittsburgh. Your plan then: Confirm the shoot is over and get a ride to the depot. You later fell asleep in inn.",
  "Tuesday 6:00 am, inn. Tuesday, February 2, 2016. The local radio plays three bright notes and announces a groundhog forecast in the town square. A delivery van backfires twice. Phil addresses Rita. Rita says: Morning, Phil. Give me a sec to get my bearings. Rita looks around. You said: Rita, it's six a.m. The radio says the groundhog's out in the square. I'm not wasting another hour. Did we wrap, or not? I've got a coach to catch. Your plan then: Confirm the shoot is done and I'm free to go.",
  "Tuesday 9:30 am, inn. Phil addresses Rita. Rita says: Morning, Phil. Stop chasing that coach. We have the weather slot booked for nine, and I am putting the town band on air at one. I need you in the studio by ten to prep the forecast. Rita addresses Phil. You said: Rita, it's Tuesday again. I need a straight answer: are we wrapped, or is the camera still rolling? I've got a coach to catch. Your plan then: Get a direct answer on the shoot status and my departure time.",
  "Tuesday 1:00 pm, inn. Phil uses the paid ticket and rides the coach all the way to Pittsburgh. Rita says: Phil, it's one p.m. We're not wrapped. I need your weather package ready by three for the two o'clock newscast, and I'm putting the town band on the back end. Let's get to the studio. Rita addresses Phil. You said: I'm done here. I'm heading to the depot. Your plan then: Get to the depot before 1:00 pm to board the coach to Pittsburgh.",

I'm just calling to make sure I'm still on for Wednesday. I'm free to help move that couch. Your plan then: Confirm my sister knows I'm in Pittsburgh and will be ready to help move the couch on Wednesday. You later fell asleep in Pittsburgh."
